WHAT TO SAY
“This project helps developers understand CI/CD failures and prepare delivery workflows. It routes tasks to a specialized agent, keeps repository changes behind human approval, and records who performed each action.”

The main demonstration

Use Developer first, then Admin. Show diagnosis, YAML generation, agent routing, real failed-run records, approval rejection, and team oversight.

The connected extension

If GitHub credentials and a reachable webhook are ready, add real log download and an approved pull request. AI chat is an optional provider-backed feature.

How to use this guide
Each feature has click steps, the evidence to point at, and words you can say. Pages 2–3 are your rehearsal checklist; page 12 is your recovery and question sheet.

DevOps.SUPERVISOR DEMONSTRATION GUIDE
STEP 1 / LOGIN AND PERSONAL VISIBILITY

Start as the Developer.

Show that the account determines access and that members work in their own workspace.

  1. Open the landing page and select Log in. Enter the Developer email and password, then click Sign in.
  2. On Overview, point out the Developer role and personal activity. Counts can change as you rehearse.
  3. Open Audit log. Show the heading Your audit log and that the entries belong to this account.
  4. Explain that Users & roles and Evaluation are Admin screens. If you open /users as a Developer, the UI shows Access restricted.
WHAT TO SAY
“The backend assigns my role after authentication. As a Developer, I see my own records and authorized approval requests. The Admin can inspect activity across the team.”
Optional signup preview
Open /signup in a logged-out window. Signup creates a Developer account without role selection. Use the existing accounts for the main demo; creating another Admin is not an available signup path.

Proof: Developer workspace, personal audit heading, restricted Admin page. The later Admin comparison makes the ownership rule visible.

DevOps.SUPERVISOR DEMONSTRATION GUIDE
STEP 2 / TRAINED FAILURE CLASSIFIER

Diagnose a sample CI failure.

Navigation: CI/CD assistant · /diagnosis · Allow about 90 seconds.

  1. Open CI/CD assistant. Under Diagnose a failure, choose the sample button npm missing test script.
  2. Point to Build or workflow log, then click Predict Failure.
  3. Show the predicted label npm_missing_test_script, the confidence, and the suggested fix. Read the score actually shown.
  4. If time allows, choose pytest not found and predict again to show a second input. Return to the npm example for continuity.
WHAT TO SAY
“This is a demonstration log. The classifier uses TF-IDF text features and Logistic Regression to identify a likely failure category. It suggests a next step; a human still reviews whether the change is appropriate.”
Interpret confidence correctly
The displayed percentage applies to this prediction. It is not the overall accuracy of the model. Short logs can produce a low score; present the result honestly and use more complete logs when available.

Proof: input → predicted label → confidence → suggested fix. This local classifier path does not need an LLM API key. If the model cannot load, run make train-model before the session and recheck the prediction.

STEP 5 / REAL GITHUB FAILURE RECORDS

Show the failed runs clearly.

Navigation: Workflow failures · /workflow-failures · Allow about 90 seconds.

  1. Open a saved run. Show the repository, workflow name, run ID, branch, status, and Recorded by. Use Open workflow run to show its actual GitHub page if internet is available.
  2. To refresh historical runs, select Import failures → Load from GitHub. Enter the repository below and click Load failed runs.
  3. Explain logs unavailable: the real failure metadata is saved, while automatic log download needs GitHub access. It is not a completed diagnosis.
Malithi2001/Autonomous-Infrastructure-Provisioning-and-Delivery-via-Agentic-AI

Optional: complete a saved diagnosis

From the failed job on GitHub, copy its genuine error log. Expand that same run in the app → Paste run logs → verify Workflow run URL → paste into Failed run logs → Diagnose and save. Show the saved label and fix recommendation. This path works without an LLM key.

WHAT TO SAY
“These are real GitHub runs. Each Developer sees their own imported records. Admin can see all owners. A run remains visible even when logs cannot be downloaded.”
Keep demonstration evidence accurate
Use the built-in sample on the CI/CD assistant for sample diagnosis. Use genuine logs from the matching GitHub run for a saved workflow diagnosis. Repeated imports reuse that account’s existing records; different accounts can each save the same run.

STEP 6 / HUMAN-IN-THE-LOOP CONTROL

Demonstrate approval by rejecting.

The local presentation can show request → review → rejection without GitHub credentials or repository changes.

  1. As Developer, open Agent orchestration. In User Command, enter create workflow pr. In Optional JSON Context, paste the example below. It uses a placeholder repository for this rejected sample request.
  2. Click Run Agent. Show that approval is required, with the proposed action and request ID. No PR has been created at this point.
  3. Open Approvals immediately. Point to requester, repository, risk level, and action. Use the fresh request you just created.
  4. Click Reject. Show the rejection feedback and the corresponding Audit log record. Rejection does not execute the GitHub action.
{
  "repo_full_name": "owner/demo-repo"
}
Request saved
Pending review
→
Human rejects
No execution
→
Decision logged
Auditable result

Demonstrate the ownership rule

Before rejecting, you can open Admin’s Approvals queue in the other browser profile to show the Developer’s request. Developer can review only their own authorized work; Admin can review team requests. User-access changes need Admin review.

If you already have a diagnosed failed run

Expand it in Workflow failures and choose Request fix PR instead. This also creates a saved approval. All fix PR writes require review, including low-risk fixes.

WHAT TO SAY
“The action is proposed first and waits for an explicit human decision. A Developer can review their own permitted work; they cannot approve another member’s work or an Admin-only access change. I am rejecting this request to demonstrate that execution stops.”
Approval is not successful execution
Approve only in the connected demo after reviewing the repository and proposed change. Then verify the execution result and actual PR URL. Expired requests cannot execute; create a fresh request when rehearsing.

STEP 7 / ADMIN OVERSIGHT AND MEMBER CONTROL

Show who did the work.

Switch to Admin · Audit log and Users & roles · Allow about two minutes.

  1. Sign in as Admin. Open Audit log and show Team audit log, tool, status, actor, timestamp, and expandable details.
  2. In Actor username, enter devops.engineer and apply the actor filter. Find the diagnosis, workflow, or approval activity from your demonstration. Confirm the username in the member list if the account has been renamed.
  3. Clear filters. Contrast the team view with the Developer’s Your audit log. Show that Admin can identify the responsible member.

Show Activate / Deactivate

Open Users & roles (page title: Members & access). Show role and status filters, account status, and Activate / Deactivate controls. Use a disposable Developer member for an access-change demonstration.

Click Deactivate → review the saved request → Reject change for a demonstration that leaves access intact. For a full access-control demo, approve deactivation, show that the member loses access, then approve activation and show that they can sign in again. Existing sessions are revoked on deactivation.

WHAT TO SAY
“Admin sees team activity and can identify who performed an action. Access changes have their own approval and audit trail. The system also protects the active administrator from being removed accidentally.”
Member creation
Add member creates a Developer. Public signup also creates a Developer. The application maintains the existing Admin account; it does not offer another Admin creation option.

OPTIONAL EXTENSION / CONNECTED GITHUB LOOP

Add live logs and a reviewed PR.

Use this extension only after a rehearsal succeeds with a repository you control.

Prepare before presentation

  • Configure backend GitHub access through a GitHub App installation or the local GITHUB_TOKEN setting. Check access to the intended demo repository.
  • For automatic diagnosis, make the backend webhook endpoint publicly reachable and configure a matching webhook secret. Keep secret values off the projector.
  • Use a demo repository and a reviewed workflow change. For AI chat, separately configure the selected LLM provider and verify a harmless request before the session.
StageWhat to click / inspectWhat confirms success

Workflow proposalCreate Workflow PR → Review approvalSaved request and proposed target repository
Human decisionApprovals → ApproveCompleted execution, not merely an approved status
GitHub reviewOpen the returned pull request URLNew branch, changed workflow file, reviewable PR
Failure ingestionA completed failed run → webhook; or Import failuresRun metadata and actual downloaded logs when available
Diagnosis / fixRequest fix PR → ApprovalsStored prediction, recommendation, explicit review and result
Webhook endpoint:
https://YOUR-DEMO-BACKEND/api/v1/webhooks/github
Current local boundary
Local GitHub log downloads and AI chat are unconfigured. Public metadata imports and local model/YAML tools work. Demonstrate live logs, webhooks, and PR execution after observing them succeed.
WHAT TO SAY
“When connected to GitHub, the same review flow creates a branch and a pull request. The reviewer inspects the diff in GitHub. The app does not directly push changes to the default branch or automatically merge the PR.”

Scope: this is a CI/CD MVP; cloud infrastructure remains future work.

DevOps.SUPERVISOR DEMONSTRATION GUIDE
RECOVERY / QUESTIONS / FINISH

Stay clear about what you proved.

Use this page if a service is unavailable or the supervisor asks about the project’s limits.

What you seeWhat to do during the demonstration
No failure rowsCheck the repository name, use Import failures, then Refresh. Developer sees only their own records; a diagnosis on the assistant page does not create a GitHub run.
Logs unavailable / unclassifiedShow the genuine run metadata. Paste the matching real job log for diagnosis, or use the assistant’s sample demo separately.
AI chat not configuredContinue with CI/CD assistant and Agent orchestration. The local classifier and YAML generation work without a conversational provider.
Expired approval / rejected requestCreate a fresh review request. Refresh the failure list before requesting another fix review. Rejected and expired actions do not execute.
Approved, but execution failedInspect the audit result and GitHub access. Do not present the approval decision as a created PR.
Backend / browser cannot connectCheck the two local servers and their ports. If internet is down, use saved runs and local model/YAML examples.

Questions you can answer directly

What is the AI component? A trained TF-IDF / Logistic Regression failure classifier; optional LLM-backed chat. Task routing in the demonstrated orchestration path uses deterministic rules.

Why multiple agents? Each request is routed to one specialist for its main task. The specialists reuse existing services and tools.

How is access controlled? Backend role and ownership checks; Developer personal records and authorized own reviews; Admin team review and member management.

What does the confidence mean? The classifier’s score for the selected label. Overall model performance is reported separately in Evaluation.

Evidence to keep ready
Admin → Evaluation: show the actual available dataset size, labels, accuracy/F1, and operational counts. Baseline verification from the preceding local check: 306 backend tests passed, lint and production build passed, and both accounts passed live browser checks. Recheck before the demo; these results do not certify unconfigured external integrations.
WHAT TO SAY
“The demonstration proves authenticated access, local diagnosis, workflow generation, specialized-agent routing, real failed-run visibility, human review, and accountability. With GitHub connected, this extends to log downloads and reviewed pull requests.”
